### Under Fire: A City in Chaos

The coastal city had known [strife]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="strife · n. 冲突；争吵；不和"} for months. What began as quiet [unrest]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="unrest · n. 动乱, 骚乱, 不安宁"} — protests, curfews, whispered grievances — had collapsed into something far uglier. Armed [rebels]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rebels · n. 反叛者; 谋反"} controlled three districts by dawn, and the government scrambled to [subdue]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="subdue · vt. 征服；抑制；减轻"} them before the situation hardened into [anarchy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="anarchy · n. 混乱；无秩序；无政府状态"}.

A [sniper]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sniper · n. 狙击兵"} had taken position on the customs-house roof, his crosshairs **stifling** any attempt to advance along the waterfront. Two soldiers tried to [resist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="resist · vt. &amp; 使用武力阻止发生；抵抗；对抗; 不受损害；抗；耐; 不屈从；经得住"} the urge to rush forward; their sergeant ordered them into a shallow [trench]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="trench · n. 沟，沟渠；战壕；堑壕; 掘沟; 挖战壕；侵害 Trench特伦奇"} and told them to wait. The naval [patrol]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="patrol · n. 巡逻；巡逻队；侦察队; 巡逻；巡查; 巡逻；巡查"} boat closed in slowly, its commander careful not to let the kidnappers [muzzle]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="muzzle · n. 枪口，炮口；口套，口络；动物的鼻口; 使…缄默；给…戴口套；封锁…的言论"} the negotiations by threatening the hostage. ### The City Before It Fell

The [warmonger]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="warmonger · n. 战争贩子"} general had spent a decade **undermining** the fragile peace, issuing one [ultimatum]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ultimatum · n. 最后通牒；最后结论；基本原理"} after another until the capital's nerve broke. On the night the [rebellion]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rebellion · n. 叛乱；反抗；谋反；不服从"} finally ignited, [bootleggers]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bootlegger · n. 酿私酒者,走私贩"} and [racketeers]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="racketeer · n. 干非法勾当者,骗子"} moved freely through the chaos, replenishing [ammunition]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ammunition · n. 弹药, 军火"} caches hidden beneath market stalls. The regime's soldiers, stripped of every moral [safeguard]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="safeguard · n. 防护措施，安全设施; 保护；保卫；防护"}, began to [slaughter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="slaughter · vt. 屠杀，杀戮；屠宰; 屠杀；残杀; 屠宰"} anyone they found near the checkpoints — yet the crowds kept surging, driven by a hunger for [vengeance]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vengeance · n. 复仇；报仇；报复"} too long deferred.

By dawn the [spearhead]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="spearhead · n. 先锋, 先头部队; 当…的先锋, 带头"} of the insurgency had punched through the northern gate. [Thrashing]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="thrashing · n. 打，殴打; 大败；惨败"} the garrison unit in a brutal [scrimmage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="scrimmage · n. 混战,并列争球"} outside the courthouse, rebel fighters seized the armory with such speed that the defenders had no time to call in air support. Officers who chose not to [surrender]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="surrender · vt. &amp; 投降; 放弃；抛弃; 投降，放弃"} fled into the old quarter and pulled on civilian [camouflage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="camouflage · n. 伪装；隐藏；掩藏; 伪装物；掩饰手段；保护色; &amp; 隐蔽；隐藏；掩藏；掩盖"}, hoping informants would not betray them. Meanwhile, handlers who had once helped the regime [surveil]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="surveille · vt. 使受监视,对…实施监视"} dissidents now faked new identities, deleting files and [tampering]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tampering"} with surveillance logs to erase their records.

The international observers who arrived at the first [checkpoint]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="checkpoint · n. 检查站,车站的行李房"} documented every [violation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="violation · n. 违反, 冒犯, 侵害; 违反; 强奸"} they could reach: the [torturing]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="torturing 拷问的;使受苦的;使痛苦的"} of prisoners in basement cells, the systematic [pilferage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pilferage · n. 行窃,偷盗"} of food and medicine from aid convoys, the [vandalism]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vandalism · n. 肆意破坏公物等德行；汪达尔人作风 Vandalism汪达尔人的行为或作风"} of hospitals and schools that bore the scars of deliberate shelling. [Pedophiles]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pedophile · n. 恋童癖者"} embedded in the militia had used the cover of war to operate unchallenged. [Accomplices]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accomplice · n. 从犯, 帮凶, 同谋"} inside the civil service had quietly [persecuted]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="persecute · vt. 迫害；困扰；同…捣乱"} ethnic minorities for years. [Smuggling]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="smuggling · n. 走私;偷运"} networks — run by the same [racketeers]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="racketeer · n. 干非法勾当者,骗子"} who had armed both sides — were already adapting, rerouting their operations before the ceasefire ink was dry.

The general, cornered in the palace, issued one last broadcast: he would [retaliate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="retaliate · vi. 报复, 反击"} against any force that crossed the inner wall. His [accomplice]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accomplice · n. 从犯, 帮凶, 同谋"} beside him — a man long known to [overthrow]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="overthrow · vt. 打倒； 推翻; 使终止; 推翻；终止，结束"} inconvenient legal processes — rehearsed the speech twice before the cameras rolled. [Watch out]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="watch out 小心；提防"}, a young interpreter whispered to her colleague; the [truncheon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="truncheon · n. 棍子; 警棍; 官杖；权杖；司令杖; 矛杆; 树干; 用棍子打，用警棍打"} blows they had taken at the earlier rally had taught them both that words here still carried real weight.

### When the Smoke Clears

The [conspiracy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="conspiracy · n. 阴谋, 密谋"} had been forming for months in the city's underbelly — a web of [complicity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="complicity · n. 合谋, 串通"} so thick that even seasoned [gangbuster]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="gangbuster · n. 〈美口〉侦破团伙者,扫荡流氓的执法者"}s struggled to untangle it. At its center stood a [tyrannical]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tyrannical · adj. 暴君的,暴君似的; 专制的；专横的"} crime lord who [intimidate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="intimidate · vt. 恐吓, 威胁"}d witnesses, [perpetrate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="perpetrate · vt. 犯,作,做"}d extortion, and relied on a network of [conspirator]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="conspirator · n. 共谋者,阴谋家"}s to keep his operations invisible. His lieutenants dealt in [counterfeit]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="counterfeit · n. 仿制品, 伪造物"} documents, [clandestine]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="clandestine · adj. 秘密的,保密的,暗中的; 秘密地,暗中地; 暗中,私下"} meetings, and [fraudulent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="fraudulent · adj. 欺骗的,不诚实的; 欺骗地"} contracts that bled the city's treasury dry.

The [insurgency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="insurgency · n. 叛乱,叛乱状态"} his rivals launched against him triggered open [belligerent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="belligerent · adj. 交战的；卷入冲突的; 好战的，挑起战争的; 交战的一方"} street conflict. The first night of fighting brought [bombardment]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bombardment · n. 炮击；轰炸"} of two rival warehouses — fire [smothering]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="smothering 封闭灭火"} the exits before anyone inside could flee. Whole neighborhoods faced the [disruption]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="disruption · n. 中断,分裂,瓦解,破坏"} of supply lines and communications; local infrastructure was nearly [obliterate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="obliterate · vt. 除去；涂去；擦掉; 彻底破坏或毁灭"}d in the crossfire. A [catastrophe]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="catastrophe · n. 灾祸, 灾难"} seemed inevitable as each faction threatened to [cannibalize]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cannibalize · v. 吃同类的肉,拆用…的配件,调拨…的人员 吃人肉,拆用配件,调拨人员"} the other's turf, stripping it bare of anything useful. One [altercation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="altercation · n. 争执"} in the market square left three men dead and [jeopardize]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="jeopardize · vt. 危及, 损害"}d a fragile ceasefire the district council had spent weeks negotiating. A [subversive]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="subversive · adj. 破坏性的；从事颠覆的; 危险分子；颠覆分子"} pamphlet, found scattered across the rubble, accused the council itself of [appeasement]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="appeasement · n. 平息;缓和;满足;姑息; 姑息政策;绥靖主义"} — choosing cowardice over justice.

It fell to an [undercover]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="undercover · adj. 暗中进行的;秘密做出的;私下的; 做密探工作的"} detective to [transgress]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transgress · vt. 超越，越过；违反，违背; 做坏事；道德败坏，违反道德；犯法"} the syndicate's inner circle. Working alone, she exposed the [oppression]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="oppression · n. 压迫手段；压抑；沉闷；镇压；苦恼"} the crime lord imposed through debt and [confinement]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="confinement · n. 限制,被监禁; 分娩"} — holding debtors in basement cells until their families paid. She caught his chief [persecutor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="persecutor · n. 迫害者"} [red-handed]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="red-handed · adj. 现行犯的,正在作案的; 手染血的; 在犯罪现场,当场; 手染血地; 当场抓住某人；现场捕获"}, mid-operation, filing a [preemptive]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="preemptive · adj. 先发制人的; 先买的;有先买权的"} raid report to corrupt officers before she could act. Her [contention]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="contention · n. 竞争, 争夺; 争论, 争执; 论点, 主张"} — that dismantling the network required prosecuting every link in the chain, not just the top — finally prevailed. When the arrests came, they were swift and total, leaving no room for the syndicate to regroup.

### Under Siege

The city had been under [surveillance]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="surveillance · n. 盯梢, 监视"} for weeks before the [confrontation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="confrontation · n. 对抗, 对抗的事物"} erupted. A [conspiratorial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="conspiratorial · adj. 阴谋的,阴谋者的"} network — funded through [embezzlement]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="embezzlement · n. 盗用,挪用"} of public relief funds — had spent months preparing. Their [premeditation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="premeditation · n. 预谋；预先设想"} showed in every detail: safe houses, false papers, [counterfeits]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="counterfeits 伪造品"} of official passes.

The [provocateur]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="provocateur · n. 奸细，内奸；破坏分子，煽动者"} at the center of the plot was a veteran of [infiltration]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="infiltration · n. 渗透"} operations, skilled at spreading [provocation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="provocation · n. 挑衅;激怒;刺激; 愤怒的原因;激怒人的事"} until ordinary men raised their fists. His methods relied on [intimidation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="intimidation · n. 恫吓，恐吓；胁迫"} rather than open force, tightening a [stranglehold]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stranglehold · n. 勒颈; 压制，束缚；严格控制"} on the district's leadership before anyone noticed the [entanglement]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="entanglement · n. 瓜葛;牵连;纠缠;缠住"}. Charges of [misdemeanor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="misdemeanor · n. 不法行为; 轻罪,小罪"} were his preferred camouflage; the graver work — [persecution]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="persecution · n. 迫害或受迫害"} of dissenters, the quiet [exploitation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="exploitation · n. 开发;开采；开拓; 利用; 剥削; 广告推销"} of the desperate — was buried beneath layers of [disobedience]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="disobedience · n. 不服从，违抗；违反"} blamed on rival factions.

When the authorities finally moved, the ring's [perpetrator]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="perpetrator · n. 做坏事者;犯罪者; 加害者;行凶者"} tried to [outmaneuver]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="outmaneuver · v. 以策略制胜,以机动性胜过"} them using [strategical]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="strategical · adj. 战略的"} withdrawals through the port's [minesweeping]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="minesweeping · n. 扫雷"} lanes, counting on [obstruction]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="obstruction · n. 障碍物，阻碍物；阻碍，阻挠; 故意妨碍议案通过; 故意妨碍议案通过者; 护栏"} at every checkpoint to buy time. But the [retaliation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="retaliation · n. 报复；反击"} came fast. Courts documented each [transgression]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transgression · n. 犯罪；违反；海侵；逸出"}, from juvenile [delinquency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="delinquency · n. 不法行为；少年罪犯; 过失，罪过"} recruited into the network, to the attempted [assassination]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="assassination · n. 暗杀"} of a magistrate, to the wholesale [destruction]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="destruction · n. 破坏, 毁灭, 消灭"} and [devastation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="devastation · n. 毁灭;破坏"} left in the wake of the final raid. The accused offered [repudiation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="repudiation · n. 拒绝;否认;断绝关系;抛弃"} of every charge; the evidence offered [anti-Semitic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="anti-Semitic · adj. 反对犹太人的,排犹的"} pamphlets, weapons caches, and a paper trail of [draft dodger]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="draft dodger · n. 逃兵役者"} payments that made denial impossible. What had begun as a shadowy [exploitation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="exploitation · n. 开发;开采；开拓; 利用; 剥削; 广告推销"} scheme ended in the most complete legal reckoning the district had seen in a generation.

### When the City Turns Dangerous

The investigation had been months in the making. Authorities suspected a mid-level official of **misappropriating** public defense funds — quietly siphoning money meant for the city's security infrastructure. Before any arrest could be made, the task force launched a covert [reconnaissance]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reconnaissance · n. 侦察或观测;巡逻队、飞行队等"} of his known associates, mapping warehouses and safe houses on the waterfront where [drug trafficking]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="drug trafficking 毒品走私；贩毒"} networks operated under the cover of shipping logistics.

Then things turned ugly. Someone inside the unit leaked the operation. The official's allies moved swiftly to **screw the lead detective over**, planting forged records and launching a vicious [smear campaign]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="smear campaign"} against her in the press. She had expected retaliation — [whistleblowing]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="whistleblowing 告密,揭发"} never came without a cost — but the speed and viciousness of it still caught her off guard. For weeks she **was subjected to** anonymous threats, surveillance, and public humiliation.

Down at the harbor, the network's recruiters worked a different angle. They would [lure wayward sailors]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lure wayward sailor"} — men adrift, broke, and desperate — into the operation with promises of easy money, cycling them into courier routes before the men even understood what they had signed on to. The youngest catches were barely teenagers, their cases eventually handed off to a juvenile court already overwhelmed with [juvenile delinquency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="juvenile delinquency 少年违法犯罪"} filings from the same neighborhoods.

The city's rot ran deep, and everyone who tried to cut it out bore the scars.
